question.problem: Use Green's theorem to evaluate ${∮}_{C}(2y-x)\,dx+(5x-y)\,dy,$ where $C$ is the boundary of the region enclosed by the curves $y=x$ and $y={x}^{2}-x.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14223852/assets/e788bbcbda4cc715c6989b7de9d08d60e3b0d178eeb9432a342a4c86c4c01b86.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=2y-x$ and $Q(x,y)=5x-y.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=2,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x} & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):0\le x\le 2,\,{x}^{2}-x\le y\le x\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}(2y-x)\,dx+(5x-y)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5-2)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}3\,\text{d}A \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}-x}^{x}\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{2}[y]_{{x}^{2}-x}^{x}\,dx \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{2}(2x-{x}^{2})\,dx \\  & =3{[{x}^{2}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =3(4-\frac{8}{3}) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
